name: Swiss / Minimalist Editorial
summary: Strict grid, one typeface family, restrained colour and exact transitions. Whitespace is structure. Meaning is carried by type scale and position.

identity.editorial_approach: a statement per frame, resolved by position
identity.composition_philosophy: asymmetric grid; empty space is a design element
identity.storytelling_conventions: build a sentence by moving type on the grid

palette.contrast_strategy: black on white with one red accent used once per frame

typography.display: Inter or a grotesque, 600-800, large scale contrast
typography.scale_and_hierarchy: 3 sizes per frame at most; ratio 4:1 or more

composition.negative_space: deliberate; at least a third of the frame

motion.grammar: Precise: type and rules move on the grid with decisive, short eases and clean holds.

timing.holds: clean stillness is intended and should be declared

transitions.continuity: a rule or baseline persists across the cut

motion.kinetic_typography: line and word build on baselines
motion.stillness_policy: Stillness is part of the style; declare intent: still so QA records a waiver.

rendering.strategy: Pure HTML/SVG/GSAP; the cheapest and most deterministic look.

provenance.method: Authored rule set (prescribed). Derived from the style system's tokens, the workspace motion vocabulary and the technique records listed; not extracted from a single reference.
provenance.notes: Every value here is prescribed intent, not a measurement. Evidence of use is recorded under 'validation' only after a render exists.

weaknesses: Easily becomes slides if every frame is a headline plus a block.
Needs real typographic judgement; defaults look generic.
No imagery means narrative load falls on narration.
example_scenes: A single large number on the grid with a rule that draws to a baseline label.
